Solution 8[edit]

We first observe the sums of the given rows:

\begin{array}{|c|c|} \hline Row & Sum \\ \hline 1 & 3 \\ 2 & 6 \\ 3 & 12 \\ 4 & 24 \\ \hline \end{array}

This sequence doubles each time, so the sum of the nth row is Setting this equal to , we get \begin{align*} 3\cdot 2^{n - 1} &= 12,288 \\ 2^{n - 1} &= 4096 \\ 4096 &= 2^{12} \\ 2^{n-1} &= 2^{12}, \end{align*} so . Thus, the row with sum is the 13th row. Next, notice that every entry in the triangle below is formed by repeatedly summing from the three numbers in the first row: 1, 3, and −1.

For example, the number in row can be expressed as \begin{align*} 6 = 1 \cdot −1+2 \cdot 3+1 \cdot 1, \end{align*} where the coefficients count the number of paths from each top entry. In general, each entry is a weighted sum of the top row, with weights equal to the number of left/right paths leading to that position.

We are searching for the value of the 3rd entry of the 13th row. From the top row to this position, there are moves. To reach the 3rd position from:
